study type: Quasi-experimental implementation study (interrupted time series analysis)
exposure: Change in intraamniotic infection (IAI) antibiotic treatment from ampicillin, gentamicin, and clindamycin to piperacillin-tazobactam
Implementation strategies including repeated education sessions and changes to electronic clinical decision support tools (eCDSTs)
outcome: Antibiotic use (days of therapy/1000 patient-days present)
cohort: The study participants were patients receiving intraamniotic infection (IAI) treatment at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.
finding: Implementing forced function changes to existing electronic clinical decision support tools, supported by stakeholder education, successfully changed IAI empiric antibiotic use by increasing piperacillin-tazobactam use and decreasing the previous regimen, without significantly altering hospital length of stay, repeat antibiotics within 14 days, or 30-day readmission rates.
